title: Quantifying the Hadamard Resilience Effect and the Coherence Gap in NISQ-Era Classifiers
summary: We report on a fundamental disparity between stochastic noise models and algorithmic performance in NISQ-era classifiers. Utilizing the ibm_kingston processor, we characterize the "Kingston Constant" ($κ\approx 0.07$), representing a 93% signal magnitude collapse. Despite this decay, we show via a hardware-calibrated stochastic digital twin that a Hadamard Test based Perceptron maintains a 93.9% accuracy for the MNIST dataset, validating our proposed Hadamard Resilience Effect under affine depolarization.
